_README.purpose: Decision tree: what the crew reports + live wearable vitals -> which Medical Checklist procedures to open, most urgent first. Used by checklist.py.
_README.REVIEW: DRAFT by Claude, 2026-11-15, for team review. Every rule cites the checklist page it is based on. Tiers and vitals cut-offs are project choices unless the source says otherwise.

inputs.symptoms: What the affected crewmember reports. Ids from clinical.py SYMPTOMS - unchanged.
inputs.signs: What a crewmate OBSERVES, or a complaint the patient reports that clinical.py has no symptom for (kind: report). Needed because the most urgent procedures - CPR, choking, seizures - are for patients who cannot report anything. Nothing here asks for a reading the wearables already give live (heart rate, blood pressure, breathing rate, SpO2, blood sugar).
inputs.vitals: Live wearable medians from telemetry.py, plus any values entered in the request. Keys: heart_rate_bpm, spo2_pct, respiratory_rate_bpm, bp_systolic, body_temp_c (thermometer only - wearables give skin temperature), blood_sugar_mgdl.

rule_schema.vitals_all / vitals_any: [{signal, lt|lte|gt|gte, rest_only?}] - rest_only skips readings taken during exercise or recovery
rule_schema.every listed constraint must hold: a rule with no constraints never fires
rule_schema.sections: ids from checklist_sections.json, in the order to work through them

_README.derived: A thermometer reading above 38.0 C counts as the fever_chills symptom, so fever combinations also fire from a measurement.

rules.reason: Not breathing: start CPR. If the airway seems blocked, use the unconscious choking procedure.
Unresponsive: open the airway and check breathing and pulse first (CPR steps 1-7). Oral airway if unconscious but breathing.
rules.source: Checklist 1-7 steps 1-7; 1-10 (oral airway, for unconscious breathing patient)

rules.reason: Choking and conscious: abdominal thrusts.
Choking and unconscious: open airway, attempt ventilation, abdominal thrusts.
Seizure in progress.
Heavy bleeding: control with direct pressure; watch for shock.
rules.source: Checklist 4-30 step 2; 1-44 (blood loss is a listed cause of shock)

rules.reason: Deep wound needing closure.
Minor cut or abrasion.
Major or electrical burn. Electrical burns can stop the heart despite little skin damage.
Head or neck injury: never move the neck; track level of consciousness every 15 minutes.
Chest injury: do not remove impaled objects; airtight bandage; listen for absent breath sounds.
Abdominal injury can cause hidden internal bleeding: monitor for shock.
Penetrating eye object: do not remove; shield and patch both eyes.
Chemical in eye: flush immediately for at least 10 minutes.
Chemical skin exposure: remove from exposure, remove clothing, irrigate.
Inhaled smoke or fumes: remove from exposure, mask on. Signs of toxicity may be delayed.
Facial or throat swelling: severe allergic reaction, rapid treatment.
Suspected fracture or dislocation: check pulse beyond the injury before splinting.
Nosebleed: 10 minutes of uninterrupted pressure first.
No pulse: start chest compressions (CPR).
rules.source: Checklist 1-7 (check carotid pulse; compressions if absent)

rules.reason: Cold, clammy skin or confusion are listed signs of shock. The wearables are already watching pulse and blood pressure.
Mild-to-moderate allergic reaction. If breathing becomes difficult or the face or throat swells, it is severe.
Red or sore eye: examine first; do not patch.
'Grain of sand' feeling: foreign body or corneal abrasion.
Loss of thermal control: the checklist covers the whole crew (fluids, skin temperature log).
These symptoms after a cabin depressurisation or oxygen drop can be altitude sickness.
Difficulty sleeping after a depressurisation is a listed altitude sickness symptom.
Back pain.
Sore throat.
Toothache.
Nasal congestion.
Upset stomach. The checklist says to use Chest Pain instead if there is chest pressure, sweating, breathlessness or arm pain.
Diarrhea.
Constipation.
Anal pain or itching.
Painful or frequent urination.
Unable to pass urine.
Genital itching or discharge.
Can't sleep.
Chest pain is in the checklist's Emergency section: vitals, chest exam, ECG.
Chest pain with breathlessness.
Shortness of breath.
Rash with breathing difficulty: the checklist says to institute rapid treatment for a severe allergic reaction.
Abdominal pain: vitals and 4-quadrant exam, contact surgeon before treatment.
Vomiting with abdominal pain: the checklist sends this to Abdominal Pain and the surgeon.
Nausea or vomiting.
Headache: the checklist sends this to Pain Relief.
Joint pain.
Joint pain with tingling is the decompression sickness pattern (CUFF class 1-3), especially after EVA or pressure loss.
Symptoms after EVA or pressure change: decompression sickness exam and treatment.
Chest pain or breathlessness after EVA is CUFF class 4 - serious decompression sickness.
Ear or sinus pain: examine the eardrum first.
Ear or sinus pain with a pressure change: barotrauma / ear block.
Rash or minor burn.
Cough.
Fever with cough.
Fever with ear or sinus pain.
Fever with a red, warm skin patch.
Fever with abdominal pain.
Oxygen saturation critically low.
rules.source: Threshold: clinical.py demo 'act' level (<92%). Procedures: checklist 1-3, 1-11

rules.reason: Oxygen saturation low.
rules.source: Threshold: clinical.py demo 'watch' level (92-94%). Procedure: checklist 1-3

rules.reason: Low blood pressure with a rapid pulse: the checklist's signs of shock.
rules.source: Checklist 1-44 (signs: pulse rapid, blood pressure low); thresholds from clinical.py

rules.reason: Low blood pressure.
Breathing rate dangerously slow: be ready to start CPR.
rules.source: Checklist 1-11 (forced O2 if not breathing), 1-6. The <8/min cut-off is a project choice.

rules.reason: Breathing rate high at rest.
rules.source: Checklist 1-3. The >24/min cut-off is a project choice (clinical.py flags >20 as watch).

rules.reason: Heart rate far outside normal at rest: attach ECG.
rules.source: Checklist 1-8. Cut-offs are a project choice.

not_covered._note: Inputs with no checklist procedure. Shown so the crew is never left with a blank screen.
not_covered.fever_chills: No standalone fever procedure. Take core temperature with the thermometer (EENT Subpack-3) and record it for the surgeon.
not_covered.weakness_fatigue: No checklist procedure for fatigue alone. Record vitals; watch for signs of shock (pale, sweating, confused).
not_covered.tingling: No checklist procedure for tingling alone. If after EVA or a pressure change, report it as such - it can be decompression sickness.
not_covered.blood_sugar_mgdl: The 2001 checklist has no blood-sugar procedure. Record the reading and contact the surgeon.
